● HOT SHOT POOL ●

A downloadable game

Buy Now$2.00 USD or more

● HOT SHOT POOL ●

The aim line is not an approximation of the shot.

It is the shot.

An original game for the Commodore 64, written in 6502 assembly.

Sixteen live balls on a machine with eight sprites. All of them moving, all of them colliding.

NEW IN 1.1
Three aim-line styles to choose from. A preview that knows a pocket when it sees one. An opponent that no longer plays itself in off. Sound effects you can keep with the music turned off, and a power bar you can actually stop where you meant to. Most of it came straight from the comments — see the full list below.

●  THE PREVIEW CANNOT LIE TO YOU

Most 8-bit pool games draw a straight guide and hope. This one traces the cue ball's actual path — the same direction tables, the same cushion mirroring and the same contact test the physics will use when you strike, stepped four pixels at a time.

Where the trace meets a ball, a second line shows where that ball departs, worked out from the real collision normal rather than drawn to look plausible. Line up a two-cushion bank and the dots go exactly where the ball goes.

IF THE LINE SAYS IT DROPS, IT DROPS.

○  A FULL RACK, ALL OF IT ALIVE

Cue ball plus a fifteen-ball rack, every one of them a real object with real momentum, on hardware that offers eight sprites. They collide with each other, not just with you — a plant is a plant, and a break scatters because the math says so.

Cushions rebound properly, the cue ball takes the angle it should off a thin cut, and balls that touch a pocket mouth go down whether you meant it or not.

◆  TWO RULE SETS, FOUR WAYS TO PLAY

Classic — clear all fifteen against the shot clock, the eight last. Eight Ball — the real rules: the table is open after the break, the first clean pot picks your group, and you must strike your own first or it is a foul.

Play it solo, against the CPU, two players at one keyboard, or set both sides to CPU and watch them play it out.

■  PLAYING FOR MONEY

Set a stake and sit down with a bankroll. A rack is a game — more pots than your opponent takes the money. The set runs until one of you is cleaned out, and there is no credit at this table.

▲  AN OPPONENT THAT PLANS

The CPU searches the angles using the same trace you see, follows the ghost line to find out whether the object ball reaches a pocket, and scores the shot by how straight the pot is. It will play a bank to get there. Set the skill and it plays the shot it found — or something near it.

CONTROLS

  • Joystick in port 2, or the keyboard
  • Aim — left/right, or A D , .
  • Shoot — hold fire or space to charge the power bar, let go to strike
  • RUN/STOP — leave a game for the menu

SCORING

100 a ball, and another 100 for every ball past the first on one shot — so a plant beats two singles. Clearing a rack pays a bonus for every shot you had left. A scratch costs an extra shot, and in Classic the eight is last: pot it early and it goes back on the table and costs you a shot for the privilege.

ALSO IN THERE

  • Original SID soundtrack, a different tune per rule set
  • Sound effects that borrow a voice from the music instead of stamping on it
  • Shot-by-shot commentary — which ball, which pocket
  • End-of-game statistics and a high score table

Sparky-D51 days ago (4 edits)

Hy again J5. About 15 minutes ago, I bought the v1.2 now. One of the friends that played your game with me, had already bought v1.0, but since you took the trouble, to actually incorporate many user suggestions now, I decided to buy it myself just a few minutes ago.  And v1.2 is a definite improvement, even though I’ve only tested it briefly so far.

It’s great, that the player can now select a straight line as the aiming-line, that makes it easier (at least for me) to judge rebound angles. Also the added SFXs really boost the game's atmosphere and the fact, that the power-meter fills more slowly now, definitely makes it easier, to control the shot-strength. The issue, where the CPU would always aim directly for the pockets, when playing against itself, also seems to have been fixed now. Therefore, good work all around.

However, I did notice one thing, even in just a few minutes of playing. Two times I had the case, that, when the players ball (you know what I mean *lol*) was surrounded by quite a few others, the aiming-line wouldn't appear, even when there wasn't actually another ball right next to me. I had to play two shots and no line showed up at all. You can keep playing then, but you have no idea at all, in which direction you're shooting then. After two more shots, the aiming-line reappeared, but naturally, I had squandered two shots.

Don't know, if this problem appears only, if the straight aiming-line is selected, because I had not tested the others so far, but there's definitely a bug here, that appears from time to time. Apart that, the v1.2 is really fun to play. If I notice another problem in this version, I’ll let you know. Cheers.

Even if I set the CPU-strength to "sharp", the computer sometimes makes senseless moves, e.g. when the black 8 is the one, closest to its own ball. And then there's the danger, that it becomes boring, because you also don't have human opponents on hand always. Cheers.

Sparky-D55 days ago (3 edits)

Today two friends and I played your game for about an hour and we enjoyed it. Nice work. However, we did have a few suggestions for improvement, that I wanted to mention. Maybe you are interested to hear?

(1) the player can turn off the music in the game, which we did, because we wanted to concentrate on the gameplay. But strangely, when music is turned off, also no soundeffects could be heard, which however, we would actually have expected, because in alot other C64 games, it's handled in a way, that, either SFX or music can be selected. But "Hot Shot Pool" sadly has no SFX at all so far, it seems and this is a bit strange while playing, when you hit the ball and when it strikes other balls and you hear absolutely nothing. It feels unnatural. SFX would create a much better atmosphere while playing, maybe you could add some?

(2) the power-meter fills up very quickly. All three of us felt, this is too fast, making it difficult, to precisely control the power, used to hit a ball, in certain game situations. 

(3) that aiming-line, shown when hitting the ball, isn't bad, but a perfectly straight line, would sometimes be more helpful, for judging exactly, where the played ball will strike next and how other balls will likely bounce off then. Would it be possible, to add a new funtion in the "options" menu of the game, to switch between that current aiming-line and a perfectly straight line? That way, players could choose, which type of aiming-line they prefer to use and I guess, that alot players will also choose a straight line here.

Besides that, it's already a good game, that makes fun. This isn't meant as criticism, just suggestions for improvement, since we’ve played a lot of pool games, especially on the Amiga-500 back then. But there are also a few good ones on the C64. Cheers.
